newsitem.title: UK: BAA says factory retailing float possible.
newsitem.headline: BAA says factory retailing float possible.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc said on Monday it would consider a share flotation for its joint venture with U.S. specialist McArthur/Glen Realty Corp developing factory outlet discount retail centres in Europe.
BAA McArthur/Glen was set up three years ago to develop sites for retailers to sell surplus branded goods at discount, modelled on the U.S. phenomenon.
Finance director Russell Walls said the venture was proving a success but the companies wanted to decide what to do when their five-year agreement ends in 1999.
"Basically there are three options," Walls told Reuters. A trade sale, a float or one of the partners buys the other out."

He declined to say whether BAA saw itself as a buyer or a seller but said the project was seen as a capital investment rather than a revenue earner. "It's a capital investment getting capital appreciation."
"You won't see us doing anything for at least a year to two years," he said. "It will depend on how successful it is. Certainly it is a hot market at the moment in these properties."
So far BAA McArthur Glen has opened three "Designer Outlet Villages", in England at Cheshire Oaks, near Chester, and at Swindon and in France at Troyes, southeast of Paris.
BAA said in its annual results statement on Monday that the sites were trading strongly and noted that the Cheshire Oaks site increased in value last year by 11 million stg to 56 million stg.
